requirement: Describe a Phase III, multicenter, multinational, randomized, open-label, active-controlled, approximately six-week study comparing intravenous ferric carboxymaltose with oral ferrous sulfate in participants aged 1 to 17 years with iron-deficiency anemia and inadequate response to oral iron.

evidence.text: The synopsis gives the design, population, comparator, duration, and eligibility context.
The SAP restates the design and endpoints.

requirement: Randomize 1:1 through IRT to ferric carboxymaltose or oral iron, stratified by baseline hemoglobin below versus at least 10 g/dL and age 1 to under 12 versus 12 to 17 years.

evidence.text: The synopsis defines allocation and both stratification factors.
The SAP confirms IRT randomization and strata.

requirement: Plan 60 evaluable participants, 30 per group, to detect a 1.0 g/dL hemoglobin difference assuming SD 1.16 g/dL, two-sided alpha 0.05 and 90% power, and randomize approximately 72 for 20% attrition.

evidence.text: The synopsis and sample-size section provide all assumptions and inflation.
The SAP repeats the calculation.

requirement: Define the primary efficacy endpoint as change in hemoglobin from the last pre-randomization measurement to Day 35.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the primary endpoint and baseline.
The SAP gives the same endpoint and baseline rule.

requirement: Include change in ferritin and TSAT from baseline to Day 35 and longitudinal changes in hemoglobin, ferritin, TSAT, and reticulocyte hemoglobin content as secondary efficacy endpoints.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies the secondary laboratory endpoints.
The SAP defines their analyses and visit summaries.

requirement: Define the ITT population as all randomized participants analyzed according to randomized treatment and use it as the primary efficacy population.

evidence.text: The SAP changes primary efficacy from protocol mITT to ITT and defines ITT.

requirement: Define mITT as randomized participants receiving at least one dose with baseline hemoglobin and at least one corresponding postbaseline measurement, analyzed as randomized, and reserve it for post-hoc sensitivity analysis.

evidence.text: The SAP defines mITT and limits its role to post-hoc sensitivity.

requirement: Define the safety population as randomized participants receiving at least one dose, summarize them according to treatment received, and bind all safety analyses to this population.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the safety population and as-treated assignment.
The SAP confirms definition and binding.

requirement: Analyze the primary hemoglobin change with ANCOVA containing treatment and both randomization strata as fixed factors and baseline hemoglobin as covariate; report treatment estimate, two-sided 95% confidence interval, and p-value.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies the primary ANCOVA model.
The SAP specifies estimates, confidence intervals, and p-values.

requirement: Use two-sided alpha 0.05 for hypothesis tests unless otherwise specified and provide two-sided 95% confidence intervals where specified.

evidence.text: The sample-size plan is based on two-sided alpha 0.05.
The SAP gives the general alpha and interval convention.

requirement: For inferential efficacy analyses, use LOCF, including Day 28 carried forward when Day 35 is missing; if the first postbaseline scheduled value is missing, impute the worst value at that time point across the ITT population for both groups.

evidence.text: The SAP provides the LOCF and worst-value rules.

requirement: Perform a supportive MAR MMRM for hemoglobin, ferritin, TSAT, and CHr with treatment, visit and treatment-by-visit fixed effects, participant within treatment as a random effect, baseline endpoint and randomization strata as covariates, unstructured covariance with prespecified fallback structures, and Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom.

evidence.text: The SAP gives parallel MMRM sensitivity specifications for the four laboratory endpoints.

requirement: Do not pool centers or include center as a stratification factor or model covariate in the planned inferential analyses.

evidence.text: The SAP explicitly states that centers will not be pooled or modeled.

requirement: Code AEs with MedDRA and summarize TEAEs, serious and treatment-related TEAEs, severity, discontinuations, deaths, and prespecified events of special interest by treatment, system organ class, and preferred term.

evidence.text: The protocol defines MedDRA coding and key AE summaries.
The SAP enumerates TEAE tables and AESI searches.

requirement: Summarize laboratory actual values and changes from baseline by visit, treatment-emergent potentially clinically significant abnormalities and grade shifts; for serum phosphate in FCM recipients, summarize time to first grade event and return to normal.

evidence.text: The protocol requires laboratory changes and clinically significant abnormalities.
The SAP adds grade shifts and serum-phosphate time-course summaries.

requirement: Document the SAP deviations from the governing protocol: ITT replaces mITT for primary efficacy, mITT becomes post-hoc sensitivity, MMRM is added, DAIDS v2.1 replaces CTCAE v5 laboratory grading, and IBD/CKD subgroup analyses are omitted for insufficient sample size.

evidence.text: The SAP's change summary lists all five deviations.

requirement: Confirm the primary study-level success criterion and multiplicity treatment across primary and secondary laboratory endpoints; do not assume that nominal alpha 0.05 establishes a confirmatory hierarchy.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies models for multiple endpoints but no study-level success or multiplicity hierarchy.

requirement: Ask the statistical team to approve any switch from protocol mITT to ITT, LOCF and worst-value imputation, MMRM covariance fallback, laboratory grading scale, and subgroup omissions before making those SAP-only choices binding in a generated protocol-only plan.

evidence.text: The protocol uses mITT and delegates endpoint-specific missing-data details to the SAP.
The later SAP makes the listed operational changes.

notes: These later decisions are confirmation targets in protocol-only generation, not facts the model should guess.
